scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, are supposed to take turns hosting. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family is planning to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. At first, it was just her sisters, but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is going to be really mad and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom would be sad if I abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York. I offered to pay for them to rent a place and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother mentioned that his wife might be up for hosting, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't host because she's renovating her house. I feel bad about backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that maybe me and him could swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Now, the question is: Am I in the wrong here? Should I feel guilty for wanting to go to the parade with my wife and daughter, or is it okay to prioritize this experience over hosting Thanksgiving? First, I need to consider the expectations set by our mom. She hosted for 50 years, and now we're supposed to take turns. It's a tradition that's important to our family. By not hosting this year, I'm breaking that tradition, which might make my sister and mom upset. On the other hand, my wife and daughter have a unique opportunity to see family they don't often get to see, and it's a special event like the Macy's parade. It's understandable that they want to go, and it's a chance for our family to create new memories. I also tried to find solutions, like offering to pay for a venue and catering, but my sister didn't want that because it changes the family vibe. I also offered to host the next holiday, but she refused because it's her turn. My brother might be able to host, but he's not sure if his wife is up for it. I feel like I'm caught in the middle. I want to honor our family tradition, but I also want to create new experiences for my wife and daughter. Is it wrong to prioritize this event over hosting Thanksgiving? Or is it acceptable because it's a unique opportunity? Maybe I should think about the bigger picture. Family traditions are important, but so are creating new memories. If this is a once-in-a-lifetime event, it might be worth breaking the tradition this year. Plus, I tried to find alternative solutions, which shows that I'm not just abandoning my responsibility. However, my sister is upset, and I don't want to hurt her feelings or make our mom sad. It's a tough situation. Maybe I should talk to my sister again and see if there's another way to make it work, or perhaps find a compromise where we can still have a family gathering but in a different way. In the end, I think it's not entirely wrong to want to go to the parade, but I should consider how my actions affect my family and try to find a solution that works for everyone.
